summary.oneLiner: Epigral delivered a record Q4FY26 (INR 736cr revenue, 23% EBITDA margin) driven by post-maintenance volume recovery and normalized operations, setting a 'new normal' baseline despite FY26 full-year degrowth. The key inflection is the impending Q2FY27 commissioning of CPVC/ECH expansions which will lift captive chlorine consumption to ~95%, structurally improving margins and insulating against external volatility.

It serves over 15 downstream sectors including pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, paints & coatings, construction, CPVC pipes & fittings, water treatment, paper & pulp, and textiles, with a small (3% of turnover) export component to about 15 countries.

currentContext.strengths: Integration depth: backward and forward integration across the chlorine value chain via a 132 MW captive power plant for Caustic Soda, chlorine integration across Chloromethanes/ECH/CPVC/Chlorotoluenes, and hydrogen integration for Hydrogen Peroxide and ECH - enhances cost efficiency and supply reliability|Locational integration at Dahej PCPIR with proximity to raw-material suppliers and logistics hubs including road/rail networks and the ports of Hazira, Nhava Sheva, Mundra, Dahej and Ankleshwar ICD|Scale/market-position claims made in the AR: largest installed capacity in at least one product line in India, on track to become India's largest ECH manufacturer, India's first bio-based ECH manufacturer, and ranks among the top 3rd-6th largest producers in India across several other product lines|Balance-sheet prudence: net debt/equity of 0.2x and CRISIL AA/Stable long-term / CRISIL A1+ short-term rating maintained despite an earnings decline in FY26|Rising captive consumption of chlorine intermediates (72% in FY25 to 75% in FY26), widening the value chain and improving capital efficiency|Growth capex funded through internal earnings rather than incremental leverage, reflecting capital allocation discipline
currentContext.strategies: Continue capacity-led expansion even through a chemical-sector slowdown, having first prioritised balance-sheet strengthening, to lay ground for sustainable growth|Scale up CPVC Resin from 75,000 TPA to 150,000 TPA (after already adding 45,000 TPA to reach 75,000 TPA), aiming to be among the largest CPVC resin capacities globally|Reduce Chlor-Alkali revenue exposure and increase the revenue share of derivatives and specialty products|Broaden the specialty portfolio via the Chlorotoluenes value chain (a first-of-its-kind integrated facility in India) targeting agrochemical and pharmaceutical intermediates as key growth sectors|Expand bio-based Epichlorohydrin capacity from 50,000 TPA to 100,000 TPA using glycerin feedstock and brine-recycling technology, targeting the largest facility of its kind in India|Deepen the Chlor-Alkali product basket (Caustic Soda, Caustic Potash, liquid Chlorine, Hydrochloric acid, Hydrogen gas, Sodium Hypochlorite, diluted Sulphuric acid) to serve chemicals, textiles, water treatment, alumina, paper and pharmaceuticals customers
currentContext.expansion: Epigral's FY 2026-27 growth agenda centres on two parallel expansions: CPVC Resin capacity is being scaled from 75,000 TPA to 150,000 TPA (incremental 75,000 TPA), targeted to make it the world's largest CPVC Resin manufacturing facility post-commissioning, and Epichlorohydrin (ECH) capacity is being scaled from 50,000 TPA to 100,000 TPA (additional 50,000 TPA), targeted to make Epigral India's first and largest ECH manufacturer; commercialisation/commissioning for both is targeted for Q2 FY 2026-27. The rationale cited includes structural demand visibility (India's CPVC demand projected to grow at ~13% CAGR on infrastructure, housing and plumbing upgrades; strong ECH demand from epoxy resins, wind energy, protective coatings, adhesives and automotive applications), deeper integration benefits (higher CPVC/ECH output increasing captive consumption of chlorine, hydrogen and caustic soda, reducing merchant exposure and improving cost efficiency), and leadership consolidation in both product lines. Capital investment has followed a phased, calibrated pattern: the Company states cumulative capital investments of Rs 2,894 Cr over the ten years ending FY 2025-26, with year-wise spending of about Rs 405 Cr (FY24), Rs 195 Cr (FY25), Rs 394 Cr (FY26) and projected spending of roughly Rs 400 Cr each in FY27E and FY28E as the CPVC/ECH expansions progress. Separately, the Company has also broadened its specialty portfolio via a commissioned Chlorotoluenes value chain (a first-of-its-kind integrated facility in India) manufacturing pharmaceutical/agrochemical intermediates, and a CPVC compound facility.
currentContext.mdna: CPVC: global CPVC pipe segment valued at USD 1.47 Bn in 2025, projected to reach USD 3.14 Bn by 2034; India's broader plastic pipes market projected to reach USD 3.65 Bn by 2034 - driven by construction activity, urbanisation, corrosion-resistant water management needs and regulatory preference for lead-free/non-toxic materials|Caustic Soda: India demand reached approximately 4.6 Mn Tons in 2025, projected to grow at a 6-7% CAGR in line with GDP growth - driven by pulp & paper, textiles, chemicals, aluminum, water treatment, alumina refining, and soaps/detergents|Chloromethanes (CMS) and Hydrogen Peroxide: Indian market expected to grow at approximately 10-12% CAGR, supported by pharmaceutical (generics) expansion, rising agrochemical demand, refrigerant gas growth, paper/textile/water-treatment adoption, and emerging solar/semiconductor manufacturing demand|Epichlorohydrin (ECH): global market valued at approximately USD 3.4 Bn in 2025, projected to reach approximately USD 5.6 Bn by 2034 (5-6% CAGR), driven mainly by epoxy resin demand across coatings, adhesives, construction, electronics, automotive and renewable-energy infrastructure, with Asia-Pacific the dominant consumption hub and a structural shift toward bio-based (glycerin-feedstock) production routes|Macro tailwinds cited by management: India's continued population growth (~1.46 Bn), rising urbanisation (urban population approaching ~675 Mn by 2035), a demographic dividend (median age ~29 years) supporting ~6-7% manufacturing growth, rising per-capita income (~USD 2,800) accelerating premium housing/auto/consumer-goods upgrades, and low per-capita chemical consumption (~USD 95-100 vs a global average above ~USD 250) leaving significant volume-expansion headroom|Global chemical manufacturing is described as diversifying away from China toward India, positioning the Company as a strategic beneficiary of this shift

risks.risk: Chemical-sector downcycle compressing margins ahead of revenue
risks.note: Management describes FY26 as 'navigating the chemical sector slowdown': revenue was broadly flat at Rs 2,542 crore (down 1%), but EBITDA fell 20% to Rs 567 crore from Rs 711 crore. Realisation and spread pressure, not volume loss, is what moves earnings, so a prolonged sector trough hits profit far harder than the topline suggests.

risks.risk: Chlor-Alkali revenue concentration in a commoditised, price-cyclical segment
risks.note: A stated key message of the report is that Epigral 'continued to reduce its Chlor-Alkali revenue exposure and increase its revenue share from derivatives and specialty products' - the company itself treats dependence on the base Chlor-Alkali chain as the exposure to be engineered down. Until the specialty mix (Chlorotoluenes, CPVC, Epichlorohydrin) scales, earnings stay levered to a commodity cycle.

risks.risk: Capacity utilisation and single-site operational disruption
risks.note: Overall production fell 4% and capacity utilisation slipped to 78% from 81%, which the Company attributes to an early and prolonged monsoon affecting a few products plus major maintenance in the first half. With 75% captive chlorine consumption, the integrated complex means an outage or weather event in one unit propagates through the downstream derivative chain rather than staying contained.

risks.risk: Handling and storage of hazardous chemicals / process safety
risks.note: The BRSR material-issues register flags this as a risk: improper handling and spills 'can cause harm to the environment or humans and also imposes a heavy fine and reputational risk on the company'. Mitigation rests on internal and external HSE audits and hazardous-waste regulations compliance. A single process-safety incident carries penalty, shutdown and licence-to-operate consequences disproportionate to its cause.

Flagged as a risk in the BRSR register: water is 'a critical input in chemical production' and water-intensive operations 'face a greater risk of operational disruption due to water scarcity, which can also increase water procurement prices and capital expenditures', while process wastewater must be treated before disposal or trigger regulatory compliance and mitigation costs. This is both a production-continuity and a cost-inflation exposure for the Dahej-scale complex.

risks.risk: Waste management and Extended Producer Responsibility compliance
risks.note: The BRSR register records waste from operations, the captive power plant and machinery maintenance as a risk, noting that 'non-compliance with waste management regulations may lead to the imposing of heavy fines'. The Company has registered under the EPR framework for plastic waste tied to its products and packaging, which converts a regulatory obligation into a recurring compliance cost.

risks.risk: Product safety, quality and downstream regulatory restriction
risks.note: The BRSR register identifies chemicals' potential health and environmental effects in the usage phase as able to 'affect consumer demand for the product and regulatory risk, which can then damage sales and lead to higher operational costs, regulatory compliance costs, and mitigation'. Mitigation is quality-control laboratories, SOPs and ISO 9001 / ISO 14001 certification - a demand-side as well as compliance-side risk.

Listed as a risk in the BRSR register, covering fraud, executive misconduct, corrupt practices, money laundering and anti-trust violations, where 'ethics violations can lead to police investigations, hefty fines, settlement costs, and damage to reputation'. Controls are the Risk Management Committee framework plus a Supplier Code of Conduct enforced through periodic assessments and audits, with statutory auditors reporting no material weakness in internal financial controls during the year.

The key inflection is the impending Q2FY27 commissioning of CPVC/ECH expansions which will lift captive chlorine consumption to ~95%, structurally improving margins and insulating against external volatility.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 736cr (Q4, +14% YoY, +22% QoQ); FY26 Rev: INR 2,542cr (-1% YoY). EBITDA: INR 169cr (Q4, margin 23%); FY26 EBITDA: INR 567cr (margin 22%). PAT: INR 82cr (Q4); FY26 PAT: INR 330cr (includes INR 81cr one-time deferred tax benefit; Normalized PAT: INR 252cr vs INR 357cr prior year). Order Book: Not disclosed (spot/contract mix). Net Debt: INR 508cr (Net Debt/EBITDA 0.9x). One-offs: INR 81cr deferred tax reversal boosted FY26 PAT; INR ~27cr mark-to-market loss on FX derivatives inflated finance costs.
guidance: Volume Growth: 10-12% for FY27. Margins: Expect to maintain Q4 levels (~23%) but no specific guidance given due to war volatility. Order Inflow: Gradual ramp-up expected for new capacities. Capex/Commissioning: CPVC and ECH expansion commissioning in Q2FY27; new greenfield project announcement expected within FY27.
order book & pipeline: Not explicitly quantified; management notes cautious ordering by customers due to price volatility, with demand picking up from May onwards.
segment / subsidiary detail: Derivatives & Specialty contributed 54% of Q4 revenue. Caustic soda ECU ~INR 30,000/MT in Q4, currently trending ~INR 37,000/MT due to West Asia conflict. Chlorotoluene ramping up post-approvals (targeting 40% utilization in FY27). CPVC/ECH running at ~65-80% utilization in Q4 post-maintenance.
growth verticals / optionality: Q2FY27 commissioning of brownfield CPVC and ECH expansions (doubling capacity) to drive volume growth. Captive chlorine consumption to rise from 75% to 90-95% by FY28. New greenfield project under due diligence for announcement in FY27 to sustain growth beyond FY29.
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 EBITDA margin normalized to 23% due to optimal plant utilization (>80%) and stable raw material costs during the quarter. Energy costs rose ~15% due to conflict; renewable share currently 8-9%, targeting 15% post-commissioning of 19.5MW wind-solar hybrid. Finance costs inflated by FX mark-to-market losses.
capex / expansion: INR 394cr spent in FY26. Ongoing projects: CPVC and ECH expansion (commissioning Q2FY27). Future: New greenfield project under evaluation.
capital allocation: Disciplined capex focused on backward integration (chlorine value chain). Net debt increased slightly to INR 508cr. Management exploring options to mitigate FX derivative risks.
risks & watch-items: West Asia conflict escalation disrupting supply chains and raw material availability. Prolonged high energy prices. FX volatility impacting finance costs (mark-to-market). Monsoon variability affecting downstream demand (PVC/CPVC).
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; emphasizes resilience via product diversification. Acknowledges uncertainty from geopolitical conflict but highlights strong operational turnaround in Q4. Conservative on specific value guidance due to volatility.
non-obvious takeaways: Finance cost spike was primarily non-cash mark-to-market loss on FX derivatives due to unexpected INR depreciation, not increased borrowing. Q4 profitability did not fully capture recent price hikes (war impact) as orders were booked prior to late-Feb escalation; benefits skewed to Q1FY27.

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).

themes.title: Industrial gases, chlor-alkali & commodity chemicals
themes.need: A capacity-led commodity-chemical and industrial-gas cycle underpins the basic-materials chain - ELLEN on air-separation/industrial gases; EPIGRAL/CHEMPLASTS/DCW/DCMSHRIRAM/GHCL/TATACHEM/GNFC on chlor-alkali, soda-ash and vinyls; LORDSCHLO on caustic; CHEMBONDCH on water-treatment chemicals. Pricing/utilization and energy costs are the near-term swing factors.
themes.driver: Caustic/soda-ash price recovery; utilization ramp on new capacity; energy-cost relief.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Not explicitly quantified; management notes cautious ordering by customers due to price volatility, with demand picking up from May onwards.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Volume Growth: 10-12% for FY27. Margins: Expect to maintain Q4 levels (~23%) but no specific guidance given due to war volatility. Order Inflow: Gradual ramp-up expected for new capacities. Capex/Commissioning: CPVC and ECH expansion commissioning in Q2FY27; new greenfield project announcement expected within FY27.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Q2FY27 commissioning of brownfield CPVC and ECH expansions (doubling capacity) to drive volume growth. Captive chlorine consumption to rise from 75% to 90-95% by FY28. New greenfield project under due diligence for announcement in FY27 to sustain growth beyond FY29.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- CPVC: global CPVC pipe segment valued at USD 1.47 Bn in 2025, projected to reach USD 3.14 Bn by 2034; India's broader plastic pipes market projected to reach USD 3.65 Bn by 2034 - driven by construction activity, urbanisation, corrosion-resistant water management needs and regulatory preference for lead-free/non-toxic materials
- Caustic Soda: India demand reached approximately 4.6 Mn Tons in 2025, projected to grow at a 6-7% CAGR in line with GDP growth - driven by pulp & paper, textiles, chemicals, aluminum, water treatment, alumina refining, and soaps/detergents
- Chloromethanes (CMS) and Hydrogen Peroxide: Indian market expected to grow at approximately 10-12% CAGR, supported by pharmaceutical (generics) expansion, rising agrochemical demand, refrigerant gas growth, paper/textile/water-treatment adoption, and emerging solar/semiconductor manufacturing demand
- Epichlorohydrin (ECH): global market valued at approximately USD 3.4 Bn in 2025, projected to reach approximately USD 5.6 Bn by 2034 (5-6% CAGR), driven mainly by epoxy resin demand across coatings, adhesives, construction, electronics, automotive and renewable-energy infrastructure, with Asia-Pacific the dominant consumption hub and a structural shift toward bio-based (glycerin-feedstock) production routes
- Macro tailwinds cited by management: India's continued population growth (~1.46 Bn), rising urbanisation (urban population approaching ~675 Mn by 2035), a demographic dividend (median age ~29 years) supporting ~6-7% manufacturing growth, rising per-capita income (~USD 2,800) accelerating premium housing/auto/consumer-goods upgrades, and low per-capita chemical consumption (~USD 95-100 vs a global average above ~USD 250) leaving significant volume-expansion headroom
- Global chemical manufacturing is described as diversifying away from China toward India, positioning the Company as a strategic beneficiary of this shift

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Q4 EBITDA margin normalized to 23% due to optimal plant utilization (>80%) and stable raw material costs during the quarter. Energy costs rose ~15% due to conflict; renewable share currently 8-9%, targeting 15% post-commissioning of 19.5MW wind-solar hybrid. Finance costs inflated by FX mark-to-market losses.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Disciplined capex focused on backward integration (chlorine value chain). Net debt increased slightly to INR 508cr. Management exploring options to mitigate FX derivative risks.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Epigral's FY 2026-27 growth agenda centres on two parallel expansions: CPVC Resin capacity is being scaled from 75,000 TPA to 150,000 TPA (incremental 75,000 TPA), targeted to make it the world's largest CPVC Resin manufacturing facility post-commissioning, and Epichlorohydrin (ECH) capacity is being scaled from 50,000 TPA to 100,000 TPA (additional 50,000 TPA), targeted to make Epigral India's first and largest ECH manufacturer; commercialisation/commissioning for both is targeted for Q2 FY 2026-27. The rationale cited includes structural demand visibility (India's CPVC demand projected to grow at ~13% CAGR on infrastructure, housing and plumbing upgrades; strong ECH demand from epoxy resins, wind energy, protective coatings, adhesives and automotive applications), deeper integration benefits (higher CPVC/ECH output increasing captive consumption of chlorine, hydrogen and caustic soda, reducing merchant exposure and improving cost efficiency), and leadership consolidation in both product lines. Capital investment has followed a phased, calibrated pattern: the Company states cumulative capital investments of Rs 2,894 Cr over the ten years ending FY 2025-26, with year-wise spending of about Rs 405 Cr (FY24), Rs 195 Cr (FY25), Rs 394 Cr (FY26) and projected spending of roughly Rs 400 Cr each in FY27E and FY28E as the CPVC/ECH expansions progress. Separately, the Company has also broadened its specialty portfolio via a commissioned Chlorotoluenes value chain (a first-of-its-kind integrated facility in India) manufacturing pharmaceutical/agrochemical intermediates, and a CPVC compound facility.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic; emphasizes resilience via product diversification. Acknowledges uncertainty from geopolitical conflict but highlights strong operational turnaround in Q4. Conservative on specific value guidance due to volatility.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integration depth: backward and forward integration across the chlorine value chain via a 132 MW captive power plant for Caustic Soda, chlorine integration across Chloromethanes/ECH/CPVC/Chlorotoluenes, and hydrogen integration for Hydrogen Peroxide and ECH - enhances cost efficiency and supply reliability
- Locational integration at Dahej PCPIR with proximity to raw-material suppliers and logistics hubs including road/rail networks and the ports of Hazira, Nhava Sheva, Mundra, Dahej and Ankleshwar ICD
- Scale/market-position claims made in the AR: largest installed capacity in at least one product line in India, on track to become India's largest ECH manufacturer, India's first bio-based ECH manufacturer, and ranks among the top 3rd-6th largest producers in India across several other product lines
- Balance-sheet prudence: net debt/equity of 0.2x and CRISIL AA/Stable long-term / CRISIL A1+ short-term rating maintained despite an earnings decline in FY26
- Rising captive consumption of chlorine intermediates (72% in FY25 to 75% in FY26), widening the value chain and improving capital efficiency
- Growth capex funded through internal earnings rather than incremental leverage, reflecting capital allocation discipline

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: West Asia conflict escalation disrupting supply chains and raw material availability. Prolonged high energy prices. FX volatility impacting finance costs (mark-to-market). Monsoon variability affecting downstream demand (PVC/CPVC).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Finance cost spike was primarily non-cash mark-to-market loss on FX derivatives due to unexpected INR depreciation, not increased borrowing. Q4 profitability did not fully capture recent price hikes (war impact) as orders were booked prior to late-Feb escalation; benefits skewed to Q1FY27.

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply chain disruption and raw material inflation from West Asia conflict; high energy costs. | Epigral Limited | beneficiary | High | Record Q4 performance demonstrates operational resilience; upcoming capacity expansions (CPVC/ECH) and high captive chlorine consumption (~95% target) position it to capture margin upside from inflated chemical prices better than non-integrated peers. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Rebranding] The company was renamed from Meghmani Finechem to Epigral in FY2024; it was incorporated in 2007 and commissioned its first caustic soda plant in FY2010.
- [Governance] 50% of the board comprises independent directors and all five board committees are chaired by an independent director; statutory auditor is SRBC & Co LLP.
- [Promoter group links] Three non-executive non-independent directors hold executive roles at Meghmani Organics Limited (CMD, agrochemicals division head, pigment division head), indicating continued promoter-group overlap.
- [Tax regime change] The company shifted to the 25.17% tax rate from FY2026, which reduced deferred tax liability by ₹81 Crore and inflates reported FY26/Q1FY26 PAT unless adjusted.
